title: Add composable RAG blocks playbook and TypeScript browser runner
author: Nikhil Rao
release_notes: Add a composable RAG playbook with block primitives and a lightweight TypeScript browser runner for local testing; no breaking changes.
description: Motivation: make it easier for developers to assemble retrieval-augmented generation flows as composable building blocks that can be previewed in the browser and used as quickstart templates. This PR introduces a 'composable blocks' playbook that documents block primitives (Retriever, RetrieverPipeline, ToolCall, Control, PostProcessor) and a lightweight TypeScript browser runner that wires a client-side shim, simulated indexing, and telemetry probes. What changed: added docs/playbooks/composable-blocks-playbook.md with examples and interactive JSON playground, added examples/ts/composable-runner/ with a tiny bundler-ready demo, added examples/ts/composable-runner/src/{runner,blocks,telemetry}.ts and a minimal webpack config, added test fixtures under examples/fixtures/composable-playbook, and updated quickstarts/INDEX.md to list the new playbook. Checklist: - [x] Docs authored with runnable snippets - [x] TS runner builds locally with npm run dev - [x] Simulated index and retrieval test included - [x] Telemetry probes emit deterministic spans for local e2e - [x] Security review: no secrets or server-side tokens in demo. Related: ENG-2145 (composable serving primitives), PM-322 (developer quickstarts initiative). Links: docs site draft https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/composable-blocks, demo preview https://internal-preview.redwood.ai/composable-runner. Backwards compatibility: no existing quickstarts changed aside from index; this is additive. Deployment notes: runner is intentionally client-only and uses a local stubbed retriever by default; guidance is in the playbook for swapping to Redwood Hosted or Dedicated endpoints. CI: added a CI job step quickstarts:ts-build-and-lint that runs npm ci && npm run build; flakiness: one test was flaky on node 16 so the CI matrix pins node 18. Followups: add a Python equivalent playbook and a GitHub Codespace template (tracked in ENG-2210).

guidance_snippet: Example: to compose a retriever + tool call block, import blocks.Retriever and blocks.ToolCall then compose with runner.compose([Retriever(...), ToolCall(...)]). See docs/playbooks/composable-blocks-playbook.md#compose for full example.
testing_notes: Local: npm ci && npm run dev starts a file-server and a simulated index. CI: headless chrome smoke validates telemetry spans and that the runner completes a 3-step scenario within 2s median latency in the matrix environment.
